questions.question: A government budget is an annual financial statement which outlines estimated government expenditures and expected government receipts or revenues for the forthcoming fiscal year. Depending on the feasibility of these estimates which of the following is **NOT** the budget type?

__
 
• Among the options, only an **Economy budget**__ is **NOT** a budget type.
 
• A government budget is an annual financial statement that outlines estimated government expenditures and expected government receipts or revenues for the forthcoming fiscal year.
 
• In India, it is a constitutional requirement (**Article 112**) that the government give a statement of estimated income and expenditures to Parliament for each financial year that runs from April 1 to March 31.
 
• This 'Annual Financial Statement' is the government's primary budget document.
 
• Budgets are grouped into three categories based on these estimates:
 
 
• Balanced budget.
 
• Surplus budget.
 
• Deficit budget.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• A government budget is said to be a **balanced budget** if the estimated government expenditures in a given fiscal year are equal to the expected government receipts.

 
 
• A balanced budget ensures economic stability if implemented successfully.
 
• A balanced budget is Inapplicable in less developed countries as it limits the scope of economic growth.
 
 
 
• A government budget is said to be a** surplus budget **if the expected government revenues exceed the estimated government expenditure in a particular financial year.
 
 
• A country's financial wealth is indicated by a surplus budget.
 
 
 
• If the estimated government expenditure exceeds the expected government revenue in a given fiscal year, the budget is considered to be a **deficit budget.**

• **A volcano is a conical hill or mountain built around a vent that connects to reservoirs of molten rock beneath the Earth's surface**__.

 __
 
• Volcanoes are formed from liquid and solid rock emanating from the interior of the Earth.
 
• A hole or vent from which molten rock and associated gases escape is also called a volcano.
 
• Volcanoes are mountains, but they are not like other mountains, because they do not result from folding and crumpling, or uplift and erosion.
 
• Volcanoes are formed by the accumulation of explosive materials such as lava and bombs.
 
• Volcanoes occur most often on Earth when tectonic plates are separating or convergent, and most of them are found underwater.
 
• Basalt, a form of lava that is typically liquid when erupted, forms most volcanoes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fault-block mountains **are formed by the movement of large crustal blocks, which are formed when stressing forces pull the crust apart.
 
• **Circum-erosional or relict or residual mountains** (Aravallis in India, Urals in Russia) are remnants of older fold mountains that have resulted from denudation. Residual mountains may also develop from plateaus that have been divided by rivers into hills and valleys.
 
• A **plateau **is a flat, elevated landform that rises sharply from the surrounding area on at least one side. Plateaus occur on every continent and occupy one-third of the Earth's landmass. They are one of the four major landforms along with mountains, plains and hills.

questions.question: A User Interface is the part of _______ that allows the user to enter and receive information.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **operating system.**

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Computer software includes both system and application software, and it's the component that enables user interaction through a user interface**__.

 __
 
• The user interface (UI) is a software feature that allows users to interact with the computer, enter commands, and receive feedback.
 
• The UI can be graphical (GUI) or text-based (CLI), and is present in operating systems, apps, and other programs.
 
• Therefore, UI is not exclusive to the operating system but spans across all types of software.
 
• Examples of software with UI include:
 
 
• Operating systems like Windows, Linux, macOS.
 
• Applications like Microsoft Word, Google Chrome, VLC Media Player.
 
• Mobile apps and development tools.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Operating System** is a type of system software that manages hardware and provides core UI elements like taskbars, file explorers, etc.
 
• **Computer Network** refers to interconnected systems that share resources but are not the source of UI themselves.
 
• **Hardware** refers to the physical components like keyboard, monitor, CPU – which are used by UI but do not provide it themselves.

questions.question: Which type of dam is a temporary dam constructed to exclude water from the specific area?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Coffer**__.

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **A cofferdam is a temporary dam constructed to exclude water from a specific area**__.

 __
 
• It is designed to allow for the construction of a permanent structure in arid environments, along with damming, diversion, or dewatering.
 
• A cofferdam is constructed of a waterproof fence by depositing sheets into a bed, which is usually steel in modern works.
 
• The walls of a cofferdam must be solid and well-bonded, to withstand the shock of hitting a heavy dredging bucket; When water is pulled out of the cofferdam, they must also be able to bear horizontal forces from the surrounding body of water.
 
• Water should not be able to enter the construction site because of the dam walls.
 
• As a result, the height of the wall must exceed the excessive water level, and it must also be waterproof.
 
• Dams are preferred in large construction sites and places with sufficient depth of dry soil bed.
 
• Permanent dams, oil platforms, bridge piers, and other structures standing in or above water are regularly built or repaired along cofferdams.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• An **impounding reservoir** is a basin built in the valley of a stream or river to contain stream flow so that the stored water can be used when supply is in short supply.
 
• A **detention dam** is a structure designed to capture surface runoff and stream water flow in order to control the flow of water in areas below the dam.
 
• **Debris dams** are a form of detention dam that collects material to keep it from flowing into locations where a substantial deposit of debris could be harmful.
